records.literal_gloss: For the director, a psalm of David.

en.L: For the director. A psalm of David.
en.B: For the music director. A psalm of David.
en.R: For the leader of the music. A song of David.

fr.L: Au chef de chœur. Un psaume de David.
fr.B: Au chef de chœur. Un psaume de David.
fr.R: Pour le chef des musiciens. Un chant de David.

sw.L: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya. Zaburi ya Daudi.
sw.B: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya. Zaburi ya Daudi.
sw.R: Kwa kiongozi wa waimbaji. Wimbo wa Daudi.

decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.
As in 4:1.
As in 3:1.

source.text: שְׁמַע־אֱלֹהִ֣ים קוֹלִ֣י בְשִׂיחִ֑י מִפַּ֥חַד א֝וֹיֵ֗ב תִּצֹּ֥ר חַיָּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Hear, God, my voice in my complaint; from [the] dread of [the] enemy you will preserve my life.

en.L: Hear, God, my voice in my complaint; \q from the dread of the enemy preserve my life.
en.B: God, listen to me as I pour out my complaint; \q keep me safe from the enemy I dread.
en.R: God, listen to me as I tell {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} my troubles. \q Keep me safe from my enemies; they frighten me.

fr.L: Écoute, Dieu, ma voix dans ma plainte ; \q de la terreur de l’ennemi préserve ma vie.
fr.B: Dieu, écoute-moi quand je déverse ma plainte ; \q garde-moi de l’ennemi que je redoute.
fr.R: Dieu, écoute-moi quand je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} raconte mes malheurs. \q Garde-moi de mes ennemis ; ils me font peur.

sw.L: Sikia, Ee Mungu, sauti yangu katika malalamiko yangu; \q uyahifadhi maisha yangu kutokana na kitisho cha adui.
sw.B: Ee Mungu, unisikilize ninapomimina malalamiko yangu; \q unilinde salama na adui ninayemwogopa.
sw.R: Ee Mungu, unisikilize ninapokueleza {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} taabu zangu. \q Unilinde salama na adui zangu; wananitia hofu.

decisions.reason: The word (siach) is used of pouring out one's troubles to God (55:3; 142:3).
The verb form can be a statement, "you will preserve", but here it is a prayer.
The word (pachad) means terror; the prayer is to be kept from what the enemy threatens.

source.text: תַּ֭סְתִּירֵנִי מִסּ֣וֹד מְרֵעִ֑ים מֵ֝רִגְשַׁ֗ת פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: You will hide me from [the] secret council of evildoers, from [the] throng of workers of wickedness,

en.L: Hide me from the secret council of evildoers, \q from the throng of the workers of wickedness,
en.B: Shelter me from the wicked when they plot together in secret, \q from the restless crowd of those who do evil,
en.R: Hide me from evil people who make secret plans. \q Hide me from the gang of people who do wrong.

fr.L: Cache-moi du conseil secret des malfaiteurs, \q de la foule bruyante de ceux qui font le mal,
fr.B: Mets-moi à l’abri des méchants quand ils complotent en secret, \q de la foule agitée de ceux qui font le mal,
fr.R: Cache-moi des gens mauvais qui font des projets en secret. \q Cache-moi de la bande de ceux qui font le mal.

sw.L: Unifiche mbali na baraza la siri la watenda mabaya, \q mbali na ghasia ya watenda maovu,
sw.B: Unisitiri mbali na waovu wanapopanga njama pamoja kwa siri, \q mbali na umati usiotulia wa wale wanaotenda uovu,
sw.R: Unifiche mbali na watu waovu wanaopanga mipango ya siri. \q Unifiche mbali na genge la watu wanaotenda mabaya.

decisions.choice: secret council: a circle that plots
decisions.reason: The word (sod) is a close circle of people who talk together, and what they decide (55:15; 83:4).
The word (rigshah) is related to the verb in 2:1, "the nations rage".
The sentence continues into verse 4, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֤ר שָׁנְנ֣וּ כַחֶ֣רֶב לְשׁוֹנָ֑ם דָּרְכ֥וּ חִ֝צָּ֗ם דָּבָ֥ר מָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: who sharpen like the sword their tongue; they bend their arrow, a word bitter,

en.L: who sharpen their tongue like the sword, \q [and] bend their arrow, a bitter word,
en.B: who grind their tongues sharp as a sword \q and fit bitter words to the bow like arrows,
en.R: They make their words sharp like swords. \q Their cruel words are like arrows.

fr.L: qui aiguisent leur langue comme l’épée, \q [et] ajustent leur flèche, une parole amère,
fr.B: qui affûtent leur langue comme une épée \q et posent sur l’arc des paroles amères comme des flèches,
fr.R: Ils rendent leurs paroles tranchantes comme des épées. \q Leurs paroles cruelles sont comme des flèches.

sw.L: ambao wanaunoa ulimi wao kama upanga, \q [na] kuvuta mshale wao, neno chungu,
sw.B: ambao wananoa ndimi zao ziwe kali kama upanga \q na kuyaweka maneno machungu upinde kama mishale,
sw.R: Wanayafanya maneno yao kuwa makali kama panga. \q Maneno yao ya ukatili ni kama mishale.

decisions.choice: tongue as a sword, word as an arrow
decisions.reason: Cruel and lying words are pictured as weapons (57:5; 59:8; Jeremiah 9:7).

decisions.choice: a bitter word: the arrow they aim
decisions.reason: The bitter word stands beside "their arrow" and says what it is.
The sentence continues into verse 5, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: לִיר֣וֹת בַּמִּסְתָּרִ֣ים תָּ֑ם פִּתְאֹ֥ם יֹ֝רֻ֗הוּ וְלֹ֣א יִירָֽאוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: to shoot in the hiding places [the] blameless; suddenly they shoot him and not they fear.

en.L: to shoot from the hiding places at [the] blameless; \q suddenly they shoot at {{gender:them|him}} and do not fear.
en.B: to fire from hiding at the blameless; \q all at once they let fly, without any fear.
en.R: They hide and shoot at people who have done nothing wrong. \q They shoot suddenly and are not afraid of anything.

fr.L: pour tirer en cachette sur [l’]homme intègre ; \q soudain ils tirent sur lui et ne craignent pas.
fr.B: pour tirer de leur cachette sur l’innocent ; \q tout à coup ils tirent, sans aucune crainte.
fr.R: Ils se cachent et tirent sur des gens qui n’ont rien fait de mal. \q Ils tirent tout à coup et n’ont peur de rien.

sw.L: ili kumpiga mshale asiye na hatia kutoka mafichoni; \q ghafla wanampiga, wala hawaogopi.
sw.B: ili kuwapiga wasio na hatia wakiwa wamejificha; \q ghafla wanapiga, bila hofu yoyote.
sw.R: Wanajificha na kuwapiga mishale watu wasio na kosa lolote. \q Wanapiga ghafla, wala hawaogopi chochote.

decisions.choice: the blameless: a person of integrity
decisions.reason: The word (tam) describes a whole-hearted, honest person (37:37). It stands for anyone such people attack, including the psalmist.

decisions.choice: and do not fear: neither people nor God
decisions.reason: They have no fear of being caught or of God's judgment (36:2; 55:20).
Balanced and Readable speak of the innocent as a group, so the singular "him" falls away.

source.text: יְחַזְּקוּ־לָ֨מוֹ׀דָּ֘בָ֤ר רָ֗ע יְֽ֭סַפְּרוּ לִטְמ֣וֹן מוֹקְשִׁ֑ים אָ֝מְר֗וּ מִ֣י יִרְאֶה־לָּֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: They strengthen for themselves a matter evil; they talk of hiding snares; they say, Who will see them?

en.L: They strengthen for themselves an evil matter; \q they talk of hiding snares; \q they say, "Who will see them?"
en.B: They make each other bold in their evil scheme \q and talk of setting traps where none can see; \q they say, "Who will notice them?"
en.R: They help each other plan evil. \q They talk about where to hide their traps. \q They say, "No one will see them."

fr.L: Ils s’affermissent dans une mauvaise affaire ; \q ils parlent de cacher des pièges ; \q ils disent : « Qui les verra ? »
fr.B: Ils s’encouragent les uns les autres dans leur projet mauvais \q et parlent de tendre des pièges que nul ne voit ; \q ils disent : « Qui les remarquera ? »
fr.R: Ils s’aident les uns les autres à préparer le mal. \q Ils parlent de l’endroit où cacher leurs pièges. \q Ils disent : « Personne ne les verra. »

sw.L: Wanajitia nguvu katika jambo ovu; \q wanazungumza juu ya kuficha mitego; \q wanasema, "Nani ataiona?"
sw.B: Wanatiana moyo katika mpango wao mbaya \q na kuzungumza juu ya kutega mitego mahali pasipoonekana; \q wanasema, "Nani ataigundua?"
sw.R: Wanasaidiana kupanga maovu. \q Wanazungumza juu ya mahali pa kuficha mitego yao. \q Wanasema, "Hakuna atakayeiona."

decisions.choice: strengthen for themselves: hold firmly to, encourage one another in
decisions.reason: The verb (chazaq) means to make strong or hold fast.

decisions.choice: Who will see them? the snares, or the plotters
decisions.reason: "Them" may be the hidden snares or the plotters themselves. Either way they think no one, not even God, is watching (10:11; 59:8).

source.text: יַֽחְפְּֽשׂוּ־עוֹלֹ֗ת תַּ֭מְנוּ חֵ֣פֶשׂ מְחֻפָּ֑שׂ וְקֶ֥רֶב אִ֝֗ישׁ וְלֵ֣ב עָמֹֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: They search out injustices: We have finished a plot well searched; and [the] inside of a man and [the] heart [is] deep.

en.L: They search out injustices: \q "We have perfected a well-searched plot!" \q And the inner [being] of {{gender:a person|a man}} and [the] heart [are] deep.
en.B: They search out crimes and say, \q "We have a flawless scheme, thoroughly thought out!" \q How deep are the thoughts and the heart of a human being!
en.R: They look for ways to do wrong. \q They say, "Our plan is perfect!" \q No one can understand the human mind and heart.

fr.L: Ils recherchent des injustices : \q « Nous avons achevé un plan bien médité ! » \q Et l’intérieur {{gender:d’une personne|d’un homme}} et [le] cœur [sont] profonds.
fr.B: Ils cherchent des méfaits et disent : \q « Notre plan est parfait, bien réfléchi ! » \q Qu’elles sont profondes, les pensées et le cœur {{gender:de l’être humain|de l’homme}} !
fr.R: Ils cherchent des moyens de faire le mal. \q Ils disent : « Notre plan est parfait ! » \q Personne ne peut comprendre les pensées et le cœur des humains.

sw.L: Wanachunguza dhuluma: \q "Tumekamilisha shauri lililochunguzwa vyema!" \q Na ndani ya mtu na moyo [ni] vilindi.
sw.B: Wanatafuta njia za kutenda uhalifu na kusema, \q "Tuna mpango usio na dosari, uliofikiriwa kikamilifu!" \q Mawazo na moyo wa mwanadamu ni vilindi vilioje!
sw.R: Wanatafuta njia za kutenda mabaya. \q Wanasema, "Mpango wetu ni kamili!" \q Hakuna anayeweza kuelewa akili na moyo wa mwanadamu.

decisions.choice: We have perfected: the plotters' boast
alternatives: they have hidden (with a change of one letter)
they have finished a well-searched plot
decisions.reason: The verb is "we have finished". It is best read as the plotters' own words. With a small change some read "they have hidden". The verse is difficult.

decisions.choice: the inside of a man and the heart are deep: hidden thoughts
decisions.reason: The plotters' minds are deep, hard to see into (Jeremiah 17:9). Only God sees there, and he will act (verse 8).

decisions.choice: a human being (B); the human mind (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of any person; Balanced and Readable use words that include everyone.

source.text: וַיֹּרֵ֗ם אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים חֵ֥ץ פִּתְא֑וֹם הָ֝י֗וּ מַכּוֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: But shot them God [with] an arrow; suddenly were their wounds.

en.L: But God shoots them [with] an arrow; \q suddenly come their wounds.
en.B: But God lets fly an arrow at them; \q in an instant they are wounded.
en.R: But God fires arrows at them, \q and suddenly they are hurt.

fr.L: Mais Dieu les frappe [d’]une flèche ; \q soudain [viennent] leurs blessures.
fr.B: Mais Dieu décoche sur eux une flèche ; \q en un instant ils sont blessés.
fr.R: Mais Dieu tire des flèches sur eux, \q et tout à coup ils sont blessés.

sw.L: Lakini Mungu anawapiga [kwa] mshale; \q ghafla yanakuja majeraha yao.
sw.B: Lakini Mungu anawarushia mshale; \q mara moja wanajeruhiwa.
sw.R: Lakini Mungu anawapiga mishale, \q na ghafla wanaumia.

decisions.choice: God shoots: what God surely does
decisions.reason: The verbs in verses 8-10 are in forms that usually tell what has happened. Here they describe God's coming judgment as if it were already done; they are rendered as present.

decisions.choice: suddenly: the plotters' own word turned back
decisions.reason: They shot "suddenly" (verse 5); now God's arrow comes "suddenly" on them. Their own weapons are turned against them (7:13-17).

source.text: וַיַּכְשִׁיל֣וּהוּ עָלֵ֣ימוֹ לְשׁוֹנָ֑ם יִ֝תְנֹדֲד֗וּ כָּל־רֹ֥אֵה בָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they made him stumble — against them their tongue; they shake [their heads], all [who] look on them.

en.L: And they make him stumble — their tongue [is] against them; \q all who look on them shake [their heads].
en.B: Their own words trip them and bring them down; \q everyone who sees them shakes their head.
en.R: What they said will be used against them, and they will fall. \q Everyone who sees them will shake their heads at them.

fr.L: Et on le fait trébucher — leur langue [est] contre eux ; \q tous ceux qui les regardent hochent [la tête].
fr.B: Leurs propres paroles les font trébucher et tomber ; \q tous ceux qui les voient hochent la tête.
fr.R: Ce qu’ils ont dit se retournera contre eux, et ils tomberont. \q Tous ceux qui les verront hocheront la tête devant eux.

sw.L: Nao wanamkwaza — ulimi wao [uko] dhidi yao; \q wote wanaowatazama wanatikisa [vichwa].
sw.B: Maneno yao wenyewe yanawakwaza na kuwaangusha; \q kila anayewaona anatikisa kichwa.
sw.R: Waliyoyasema yatatumiwa dhidi yao, nao wataanguka. \q Kila anayewaona atawatikisia kichwa.

decisions.choice: they make him stumble: their own words bring them down
alternatives: they make it (their tongue) a stumbling block for them
decisions.reason: The line is hard. It seems to mean that what the wicked said brings their own ruin; "him" is each of them.

decisions.choice: shake: shake the head in scorn
decisions.reason: The verb (nud) is used of shaking the head at someone's downfall (Jeremiah 48:27); it can also mean to flee.
Balanced and Readable keep the plural (m1).

source.text: וַיִּֽירְא֗וּ כָּל־אָ֫דָ֥ם וַ֭יַּגִּידוּ פֹּ֥עַל אֱלֹהִ֗ים וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֥הוּ הִשְׂכִּֽילוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they feared, all humankind, and they declared [the] deed of God, and his work they understood.

en.L: And all humankind fears; \q and they declare the deed of God, \q and they understand {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work.
en.B: Then everyone is struck with awe; \q they announce what God has done \q and think deeply about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deeds.
en.R: Then everyone is filled with fear. \q They tell others what God has done, \q and they think about it carefully.

fr.L: Et tous {{gender:les humains|les hommes}} craignent ; \q et ils proclament l’œuvre de Dieu, \q et ils comprennent {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} action.
fr.B: Alors tout le monde est saisi de crainte ; \q on annonce ce que Dieu a fait \q et on médite sur {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} actes.
fr.R: Alors tout le monde est rempli de crainte. \q Ils racontent aux autres ce que Dieu a fait, \q et ils y réfléchissent avec attention.

sw.L: Na wanadamu wote wanaogopa; \q nao wanatangaza tendo la Mungu, \q nao wanaielewa kazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Ndipo kila mtu anajaa hofu takatifu; \q wanatangaza yale Mungu aliyoyatenda \q na kuyatafakari kwa kina matendo {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Ndipo kila mtu anajaa hofu. \q Wanawaambia wengine yale Mungu aliyoyatenda, \q nao wanayafikiria kwa makini.

decisions.reason: The fear is the awe people feel when they see God act (40:4).
As in verse 8, the past forms describe what will surely happen; they are rendered as present.

source.text: יִשְׂמַ֬ח צַדִּ֣יק בַּ֭יהוָה וְחָ֣סָה ב֑וֹ וְ֝יִתְהַֽלְל֗וּ כָּל־יִשְׁרֵי־לֵֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: Let him rejoice, [the] righteous, in YHWH and take refuge in him; and let them boast, all [the] upright of heart.

en.L: Let the righteous rejoice in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and take refuge in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q and let all the upright of heart boast.
en.B: May the righteous be glad in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} their refuge; \q may all whose hearts are true give praise.
en.R: May people who do what is right be glad because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q May they run to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for safety. \q May all whose hearts are honest celebrate!

fr.L: Que le juste se réjouisse {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et se réfugie en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ; \q et que tous ceux qui ont le cœur droit se glorifient.
fr.B: Que le juste soit dans la joie à cause {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et fasse de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} son refuge ; \q que tous ceux qui ont le cœur droit chantent {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} louange.
fr.R: Que ceux qui font ce qui est juste soient heureux à cause {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. \q Qu’ils courent vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour être en sécurité. \q Que tous ceux qui ont le cœur honnête fassent la fête !

sw.L: Mwenye haki na amfurahie {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kukimbilia {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}; \q na wote walio wanyofu wa moyo wajivune.
sw.B: Wenye haki na wafurahi katika {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kumfanya {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kuwa kimbilio lao; \q wote ambao mioyo yao ni ya kweli na wamsifu.
sw.R: Watu wanaotenda yaliyo haki na wafurahi kwa sababu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Na wakimbilie {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} ili wawe salama. \q Wote wenye mioyo ya unyofu na washangilie!

decisions.reason: The upright boast not in themselves but in what God has done (34:3).
The verbs can be wishes or statements; at the end of the psalm they call the righteous to rejoice.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says what taking refuge means.
